title: CI PP_DEBUG compile gate covers only the app; the PP_DEBUG-gated harness files (overlay.odin + the overlay-check verb) compile in no CI step
evidence: ci.yml:99-104: "# Story 5.7 (W10, Perkins r1): the PP_DEBUG overlay build must stay / # compile-green in CI — two whole files rot silently otherwise. The / # overlay is compile-gated, so this build also proves the gate itself / # holds (the plain build above proves the release shape). / - name: PP_DEBUG overlay build (compile gate) / run: odin build app -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:app-debug.bin" — harness/overlay.odin:23: "when #config(PP_DEBUG, false) {" (wraps the entire 139-line file); harness/main.odin:82: "when #config(PP_DEBUG, false) { if verb == \"overlay-check\" {". `grep -rn PP_DEBUG .github/ tools/` shows no other build step.
detail: The W10 gate's own comment says it prevents 'two whole files' from rotting — the two fully gated files are app/render/debug_overlay.odin and harness/overlay.odin — but `odin build app` never compiles harness/overlay.odin or main.odin's gated verb; a render-API rename would rot them CI-silently.
recommended_fix: Add a CI step building the PP_DEBUG harness too, e.g. `ODIN_ROOT=tools/raylib-sw/shadow odin build harness -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:bin/harness-debug` (compiles green locally today).

title: PR body cites a stale '555KB' pause stats stream; the stream at this sha is 369,452 bytes
evidence: _pr_body.md:93: "boot, pause (5.3 schedule, 555KB), ecmp, surge (crisis re-fire), health_lose" — actual run at this sha: `./bin/harness stats-check pause` prints (via harness/stats.odin:80 `fmt.printf("  stats %-20s live == replay (%d bytes, byte-identical)\n", demo, len(live))`) "stats pause live == replay (369452 bytes, byte-identical)". No pause artifact measures 555KB (goldens/pause.log.bin = 90 B, pause.t1 = 43,039 B); r1's core/stats.odin (6b09497) had no D-row find-or-append aggregation, so r2's W6 fix shrank the stream after the figure was written.
detail: Stale r1-era size figure left in the r2 PR body — the same artifact-vs-prose drift class r1 flagged (W3). The byte-verified tick-21 excerpt is correct; this parenthetical is not.
recommended_fix: Update the PR body parenthetical to the measured size (369,452 bytes ≈ 361 KiB) or drop the size claim.

title: Dead `before := len(state.events)` / `_ = before` captures left in two stats_test loops after the r2 value-pin rework
evidence: core/stats_test.odin:124-132: "for tick in u64(1)..=12 { / before := len(state.events) / batch := make([dynamic]Command, 0, 4, context.temp_allocator) / ... / step(&state, tick, batch[:], &cat) / _ = before / clear(&state.events)" — identical pattern at 258-266 ("for tick in u64(1)..=20 { / before := len(state.events) / ... / _ = before"). The r2 value-pin rework calls stats_compute once after the loop, so `before` is never read.
detail: The event-mark capture was needed by r1's per-tick hash emission; the rework dropped that use but left the capture plus an explicit discard — dead code in the new file.
recommended_fix: Delete the `before := len(state.events)` and `_ = before` lines from both loops in test_stats_derivation_congested and test_stats_bundle_member_replication.

title: fmt_tmp shim's comment claims 'the render package has no fmt strings'; four sibling render modules already format via fmt.aprintf
evidence: debug_overlay.odin:283-287: "// fmt_tmp — a tiny temp-allocated printf shim (the render package has no fmt / // strings; the harness frees the temp arena per tick — these strings die with / // the frame, exactly like the render package's other per-frame strings). / fmt_tmp :: proc(format: string, args: ..any) -> string { / return fmt.tprintf(format, ..args) }" — contradicting siblings, e.g. app/render/forecast.odin:81: "mult := fmt.aprintf("x%d", f.multiplier, allocator = context.temp_allocator)" and health.odin:44: "pct_txt := fmt.aprintf("%d%%", health.meter_pct, allocator = context.temp_allocator)".
detail: The comment misstates the package's established idiom (direct fmt.aprintf with explicit temp allocator in forecast/health/crisis/assist); the shim introduces a second formatting path under a false premise.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment (siblings use fmt.aprintf), or drop fmt_tmp and call fmt.aprintf(fmt, ..., allocator = context.temp_allocator) directly like the other render modules.
